new_statements.quote: Although a few words are distinguished by high vs. low tone, Fa d’Ambô seems to no longer be a tone language. The accent normally falls on the penultimate syllable and except for these few words no tone differentiation is made.
new_statements.citation: Post, Marike. 2013. Fa d'Ambô. In Susanne Maria Michaelis, Philippe Maurer, Martin Haspelmath & Magnus Huber (eds.), The survey of pidgin and creole languages, vol. 2: Portuguese-based, Spanish-based, and French-based languages, 81-89. Oxford: Oxford University Press. Read as APiCS Online survey chapter 38 (https://apics-online.info/surveys/38).
new_statements.locator: §4 Phonology (online chapter; printed version vol. 2 pp. 81-89, exact page not determinable from the online text)
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word accent normally falls on the penultimate syllable; a residual lexical high/low tone contrast survives on a handful of words only, and long-vowel syllables carry a rising (LH) pitch whether or not they are stressed. The older primary description (Vila 1891, 'Prosodia', saved) refines this in a Portuguese-like way: vowel-final words of two or three syllables are penult-stressed, but verbs (and many adverbs) are always oxytone and consonant-final words are oxytone; the stress-marked transcriptions in Silveira et al. 2013 (pp. 31-32) match Vila ([ˈgula], [ˈbu:du] vs. verbs [lɛ:ˈva], [xõˈta], [mu:ˈta] and [xaˈsol] 'dog'). So 'penult' is the default for vowel-final non-verbs, with a lexical-class/final-consonant conditioned final-stress pattern.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in any opened source.
new_statements.exceptions: Post: 'a few words' distinguished by high vs low tone; long-vowel syllables always rising tone regardless of stress. Vila 1891: verbs and many adverbs oxytone (amoyá, amapassá, danjí); consonant-final words oxytone (vigil, tambol). Silveira et al. 2013 (pp. 40-41): in yes/no questions stress may shift to the last mora of the final word ('acentue a última mora... mesmo se a palavra não possuir acento final') together with rising intonation.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (citation forms) in Post and Vila; the interrogative stress shift in Silveira et al. 2013 is a phrase-final/intonational process. Fa d'Ambô is described as a residually tonal language (APiCS feature 120: simple lexical tone system), so 'accent' here is stress-like prominence coexisting with marginal lexical tone.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources describe Fa d'Ambô proper (fada1250) as spoken on Annobón (and by the Malabo diaspora); Post's APiCS chapter documents the Annobón lect. Vila 1891 calls it 'Ambú'; Schuchardt 1888 'Negerportugiesisch von Annobom'. No dialect split relevant to stress is reported.

sources.note: §4 Phonology: 'Although a few words are distinguished by high vs. low tone, Fa d'Ambô seems to no longer be a tone language. The accent normally falls on the penultimate syllable and except for these few words no tone differentiation is made.' Long-vowel syllables are not obligatorily stressed but carry a rising (LH) tone, e.g. [pátu] H-H 'bird' vs [pá:tu] LH-H 'plate'. APiCS structure dataset feature 120 Tone = 'Simple system, for lexical distinctions only' (source Post 1994: 194).

sources.citation: Vila, Isidro. 1891. Elementos de la gramática Ambú ó de Annobón. Madrid: A. Pérez Dubrull. (Rosetta Project excerpt: title page + 'Pronunciación' pp. 7-8 and 'Prosodia'.)
sources.note: 'Prosodia' (p. 8/9; the excerpt crops the page number, the preceding page is 8): '1.ª Los verbos se pronuncian agudos siempre. También se pronuncian así muchos adverbios, como amoyá, amapassá, danjí, etc. Para distinguirlos, llevan acento en la última sílaba. 2.ª Las palabras de dos ó tres sílabas, acabadas en vocal, se pronuncian según las reglas del español, como panu, lunga, primelu, etc. Si acaban en consonante son agudas, como vigil, tambol, etc.' = verbs (and many adverbs) final-stressed; vowel-final 2-3-syllable words penult (Spanish default); consonant-final words final.

sources.note: §4.2 Fonologia (p. 31): no stress rule stated; 'O sistema tonal não será abordado neste trabalho.' Stress-marked transcriptions pp. 31-32 show penult stress in vowel-final nouns ([ˈgula], [ˈfisu], [ˈbu:du]), final stress in verbs ([lɛ:ˈva] 'enamorar-se', [xõˈta] 'narrar', [mu:ˈta], [tu:ˈka:]) and in consonant-final words ([xaˈsol] 'cão'); 'a quantidade vocálica não está associada à tonicidade' (p. 32). pp. 40-41: yes/no questions can be marked by shifting stress to the last mora of the final word ('acentue a última mora (vogal ou glide) da última palavra, mesmo se a palavra não possuir acento…
